transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Clara Wu (Redwood CSM); Jordan Blake (SeraphTech Head of Legal), Rita Gomez (CTO), Marcus Yeo (Procurement), Samir Patel (Security)

Summary: quick procurement review, MSA/DPA redline requests, SLA thresholds and credits discussion, pricing band for Dedicated capacity pilot, and onboarding/pricing signoffs.

[00:00] Ethan: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have folks on from legal and procurement, appreciate you making time. quick introductions?
[00:08] Jordan: Jordan Blake, head of legal at SeraphTech, hello.
[00:11] Rita: Rita, CTO.
[00:13] Marcus: Marcus procurement.
[00:15] Samir: Samir, security.
[00:18] Ethan: Great. Priya is our solutions engineer, she'll cover SLA and pilot benchmarks. Clara's here for onboarding and contracts.
[00:25] Priya: Hey all, hi. I'll keep it technical but high level.
[00:28] Jordan: Thanks. We circulated the MSA and DPA draft; we have several redline requests. Wanted to walk through expectations for indemnity, data residency, and breach notification timelines.
[00:40] Ethan: Totally, Jordan. We saw your comments in the doc, we'll send a redlined copy back. High level, Redwood's standard MSA has clauses for liability caps and indemnity that are negotiable depending on enterprise terms.
[00:52] Jordan: The liability cap is a sticking point 	6 they want it at 12 months of fees, but our legal prefers 6 months for SaaS vendors although we recognize inference spend can be large. Is there flexibility?
[01:05] Ethan: There's some room; for Dedicated/Private customers we often move to 9 months or carveouts for gross negligence. We can propose 9 months and explicit carveouts.
[01:15] Jordan: Okay, that helps. On DPA, we need to ensure KMS integration and customer-managed keys for PII. We also need clarity on data retention and ability to delete training data.
[01:28] Priya: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and can ensure keys are customer-controlled. For Hosted API, we have bring-your-own-key options in limited regions 	6 but for your compliance profile it sounds like Private or Dedicated with VPC and KMS is the safe path.
[01:45] Samir: We need logs and audit trail retention 	6 SOC2 evidence and log export. What's typical retention window?
[01:53] Clara: We can offer audit log export and retain logs per the enterprise package, standard retention is 90 days in the console, extended retention available as add-on. We'll include the log export mechanics in the security pack.
[02:05] Marcus: Procurement question 	6 pricing tiers in the worksheet show pilot at lower committed tokens, but our finance needs a clear escalation to production pricing. do you have an example PO and commitment cadence?
[02:18] Priya: Yes, typically pilot is 30	690 days with a committed minimal monthly spend for Dedicated. We provided a sample tier: Pilot (30k tokens/day), Prod (100k+ tokens/day) with discounted per-token rates once thresholds reached. We'll share an explicit pricing spreadsheet.
[02:33] Marcus: We also need to understand SLA uptime and credits; our vendor risk team requires 99.95% for inference endpoints, with service credits and response SLAs.
[02:45] Ethan: Our Dedicated SLA target is 99.95% with a defined credit table; for Private deployments we can negotiate SLA tiers depending on infra ownership. Priya, do you want to walk through the SLA worksheet?
[02:58] Priya: Sure. So 99.95% corresponds to about ~22 minutes/month of downtime allowed; credit levels escalate based on monthly downtime bands. We also track p50/p95 latency SLOs and can define remediation steps 	6 automatic fallback to hosted model variants to mitigate outages if configured.
[03:20] Jordan: We need the credit calculation spelled out in the MSA. And also an escalation path 	6 24x7 support contact for severity one incidents.
[03:29] Ethan: Agreed, we'll include the full credit calc and the 24x7 support contact for Sev-1. For the MSA we'll add an escalation matrix.
[03:36] Samir: On data residency, SeraphTech operates in EU and US 	6 any cross-region replication? Our DPA needs explicit residency controls and subprocessor list.
[03:46] Priya: We provide region pinning for Dedicated and Private; hosted tiers may replicate for DR, but we can restrict region replication for enterprise customers. We'll provide subprocessor list in the security pack and the DPA will enumerate residency guarantees.
[04:00] Rita: For KMS options, if we run Private on-prem we want full control; if Dedicated in cloud, we'd like BYOK.
[04:08] Priya: Both supported 	6 Private gives you on-prem KMS; Dedicated supports BYOK in supported cloud regions. We'll note supported regions in the DPA appendix.
[04:18] Jordan: Back to liability: exceptions for data breach caused by vendor negligence are acceptable, but we need the right to audit for compliance annually.
[04:27] Ethan: Redwoods standard includes audit rights for enterprise; we can include annual audit terms and specifics on scope.
[04:33] Jordan: Great. Marcus, timeline from procurement?
[04:36] Marcus: If legal signoff is by next Friday and pricing is within the expected band, we can issue PO in 2 weeks; finance needs a quote and the vendor risk pack.
[04:45] Ethan: We'll prioritize the redlines and security pack. Clara will open the trial and share the quote.
[04:50] Clara: I'll open the trial today and invite the team 	6 expect invite by EOD.
[04:55] Priya: Pilot scope 	6 suggested benchmark: 30k tokens/day, 90k interactive calls/day, 95th percentile latency under 350ms on Dedicated GPUs. We'll run a synthetic load and also a small real-workload run.
[05:08] Rita: That latency target seems aggressive; what's been typical in prior pilots?
[05:12] Priya: For similar customers we've seen p95 ~250	6400ms on well-optimized models on Dedicated. It depends on batch sizes and prompt shapes; we'll help tune.
[05:22] Ethan: Also, cost controls 	6 we recommend prefix caching and batching settings to reduce token spend; Redwood Optimize will give suggestions.
[05:30] Marcus: On billing, we need invoicing to align to monthly PO. do you accept net-30?
[05:34] Ethan: Net-30 is standard for enterprise; we can accommodate net-45 or net-60 for larger contracts but that will be reflected in pricing.
[05:42] Jordan: Any subcontractors or subprocessors? We need list for DPA.
[05:47] Priya: We'll include subprocessors (cloud infra providers, monitoring) in the security pack; all will be listed in the DPA appendix.
[05:55] Samir: Pen test evidence?
[05:58] Clara: We'll share SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and the vendor security questionnaire responses.
[06:05] [small cross-talk] Marcus: ok good.
[06:10] Ethan: Quick note on fallback behaviors: if a model variant is unhealthy we can route to a compatible lower-capacity model to avoid total outage 	6 helps meet availability.
[06:20] Priya: This is configurable in the routing policy 	6 latency vs cost tradeoffs. We can show a route demo during the pilot.
[06:29] Jordan: One more legal point 	6 IP ownership of prompts/output, we want explicit statement that SeraphTech retains ownership of our prompts and any customer data, and Redwood may not use customer prompts to train models.
[06:42] Ethan: Redwood's policy for enterprise accounts: customer data and prompts are not used for model training; we'll put that guarantee and the data usage clauses into the DPA and MSA.
[06:52] Rita: Great. Marcus, what's your gating item?
[06:55] Marcus: Pricing approval and a clear PO template. If we can get the redlined MSA and a quote by end of week, we can get internal approvals.
[07:05] Ethan: We'll do that. Clara, confirm trial account and quote.
[07:09] Clara: Confirmed.
[07:12] Priya: For the pilot plan I'll propose test cases: 1) synthetic throughput test, 2) end-to-end app integration test, 3) latency profiling. We'll document expected KPIs.
[07:24] Jordan: Please include data handling steps in the pilot plan.
[07:28] Priya: Yep.
[07:30] [15:00 timestamp later in call] [15:03] Priya: A couple of gotchas 	6 if you want guaranteed 99.99% we need additional redundancy and that pushes cost up; most customers choose 99.95% to balance cost.
[15:18] Jordan: We'll review that tradeoff.
[15:30] Marcus: One procurement item 	6 do you have an MSP or reseller? We prefer vendor on invoice directly.
[15:36] Ethan: We invoice directly; reseller agreements are possible but not necessary here.
[15:40] [20:00 mark] [20:05] Samir: Security question on encryption at rest for logs 	6 are logs encrypted with customer keys?
[20:12] Priya: Logs in enterprise Dedicated can be encrypted with customer-managed keys; hosted offerings will use Redwood-managed keys unless BYOK is requested and available in region.
[20:22] Jordan: On audits 	6 do you allow third-party audits?
[20:26] Ethan: We support scheduled third-party audits for enterprise customers under NDA and scope; we can include audit cadence in the MSA.
[20:34] [28:00 mark] [28:05] Marcus: timeline recap 	6 legal redlines by Friday, pricing spreadsheet by Friday, Clara to spin up trial today, pilot kickoff target week of Aug 3.
[28:20] Ethan: Yes. We'll also include a demo of the routing/fallback and show SLA calc in writing.
[28:29] Jordan: Please send the MSA redline as track changes; legal prefers that format.
[28:33] Clara: noted.
[28:36] [final minutes] [35:00] Ethan: quick recap of next steps: send redlines, share SLA worksheet/pricing, open trial, schedule pilot kickoff. Anything else?
[35:12] Rita: No, that's it from engineering.
[35:14] Marcus: That works.
[35:16] Jordan: We'll review redlines and aim for signoff.
[35:20] Ethan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs.
[35:25] [meeting ends]

References shared on call: MSA draft link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/contracts/MSA/seraph-draft (shared post-call), SLA worksheet (will be attached), Security pack (link to SOC2/pen test summary).

Notes on transcription quality: occasional overlaps and small mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., "KV cache" vs "K V cache"), speaker labels approximate.

End of transcript.
